description: We are a team dedicated to tackling the "Space Mission Design Game" challenge. Our goal is to develop an interactive, web-based simulation game that demonstrates real-world space mission planning, balancing engineering trade-offs, resource management, and orbital trajectories using NASA open data. We are focused on delivering a playable, engaging, and science-grounded experience within 48 hours.
summary: We developed an interactive 3D spaceflight simulation that lets users design, assemble, and launch spacecraft across historic milestones and future exploration—spanning the foundational 2014 lunar flight test, NASA's Artemis I and II missions, and a forward-looking Artemis III scenario featuring Orion, SpaceX Starship HLS, and Blue Moon orbital rendezvous. Traditional space education often relies on static theory, making aerospace engineering, multi-vehicle docking, and orbital mechanics difficult to grasp. Powered by official NASA datasets and real orbital calculations, our application bridges past breakthroughs with humanity's future return to the Moon, making complex spaceflight learning engaging, visual, and accessible for everyone.
details:
What Does It Do & How Does It Work?Spacelogs is an interactive 3D space mission visualization and orbital simulation web application designed to bring complex deep-space trajectories to life directly in the browser. Through a modular data-adapter architecture, the platform processes orbital trajectory coordinates—including NASA JPL Horizons data—and renders multi-spacecraft missions in real time. Users can explore dedicated scenarios such as Artemis I, Artemis II, Artemis III, Lunar 2014, and an open Sandbox mode. In the Artemis III scenario, Spacelogs models the trajectories, orbital stages, and docking maneuvers of three distinct spacecraft: NASA’s Orion (orange trajectory), SpaceX Starship HLS (blue trajectory), and Blue Origin Blue Moon (purple trajectory). Users can scrub through mission timelines, adjust playback speeds, monitor live telemetry (X/Y/Z coordinates, velocity, gravity, mission elapsed time, and system status), and dynamically switch viewpoints using an interactive CameraRig targeting Earth, Orion, Starship, or Blue Moon.

Benefits & Intended Impact Space mission data is often locked behind dense tables, static diagrams, or complex astrodynamics software. Spacelogs bridges that gap by turning real orbital mechanics and mission timelines into an intuitive, visual, and interactive experience. Our intended impact is to democratize space exploration literacy—helping students, educators, and space enthusiasts intuitively grasp multi-vehicle mission architectures, Translunar Injection (TLI), lunar orbit rendezvous, and deep-space navigation without needing specialized desktop software.

Tools, Languages, Software & Hardware Used

  • Languages & Core Web Technologies: JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, CSS3
  • Frameworks & 3D Graphics: React, Three.js (for real-time 3D rendering, orbital path lines, planetary lighting, and interactive camera rigs), Vite
  • Data & Astrodynamics: NASA JPL Horizons orbital data and custom modular mission stage adapters
  • Development Tools & Hardware: Git & GitHub for version control, Visual Studio Code, and consumer laptops for local development and WebGL performance testing

Creativity & Innovation Rather than displaying a single static trajectory line, Spacelogs combines a multi-vehicle 3D orbital viewer with a mission-control-style live telemetry HUD and timeline scrubber. Color-coded trajectories, docking markers, and instant target-switching cameras let users experience complex multi-agency architectures—like Artemis III’s coordination between Orion, Starship HLS, and Blue Moon—from multiple perspectives in a single cohesive interface.

Key Factors Considered by Our Team

  • Accessibility & Performance: We built Spacelogs as a lightweight, browser-based WebGL application so anyone can run smooth 3D simulations on standard laptops without heavy installations.
  • Modularity & Scalability: By separating mission datasets into standardized scenario adapters, new missions and spacecraft trajectories can be integrated cleanly without rewriting the core 3D rendering engine.
  • Clarity vs. Realism: We balanced authentic orbital parameters and mission stages (from Low Earth Orbit to Translunar Injection and lunar arrival) with clear visual cues, color coding, and readable telemetry panels so users never feel overwhelmed by raw data.
